title: Execution of a counter update
statement: Let $A,B,N,n,t,T$ be natural numbers, let $l$ be a list of integers, let $\mu$ be an integer-valued memory, and let $Q$ be a state predicate. Suppose $Q$ holds in the state whose locals are the frame obtained by setting local $B$ to $(t+1)\bmod n$ and then local $A$ to $(t+1)/n$ in $l$, and whose memory is $\mu$. If $0<n$, $t+1$ and $n$ are at most the word limit, the initial frame has values $t/n$, $t\bmod n$, and $n$ at locals $A,B,N$, respectively, $A\ne B$, $B\ne N$, and $14\le T$, then the statement that increments $B$, resets it to zero and increments $A$ when the new value of $B$ equals $N$, has an execution from the state with frame $l$ and memory $\mu$, with cost at most $T$, ending in a state satisfying $Q$.
